svg.aria-label: How to write 饼: 9 strokes · 8 pen lifts · 9 movements
svg.title: Writing 饼
svg.desc: 9 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 饼 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 饼.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E9%A5%BC.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 饼, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the food piece as 饭 opens: a left-falling stroke, a short horizontal that hooks down to the left without lifting, then a vertical that flicks up to the right. Medians 4–9 draw the right side: a dot and a short left-falling stroke leaning toward each other, two horizontals, the lower one longer, a left-falling stroke down the left, then a long vertical down the right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
